subject: PayGrid model-fit evaluation & parity thresholds
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: PayGrid model-fit evaluation - next steps

Hi Samir —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the model-fit eval started: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary goal: replace current proprietary NLU baseline for invoice parsing and classification while keeping QA/hallucination risk at or below current levels.
- Key success metrics: task accuracy (macro F1) and hallucination rate on the operational prompt set.

Recommended initial model slate (open models we suggest testing)
- Llama-3-70B-chat (quantized 4-bit) — strong in contextual reasoning and instruction-following.
- RedOpen-13B-v2 (optimized 8-bit) — good latency/cost tradeoff for high-throughput endpoints.
- RedOpen-7B-Chat (int8) — baseline low-cost option for sanity checks.

Parity / acceptance thresholds (proposal)
- Quantitative: <= 5% absolute drop in task accuracy (macro F1) vs your proprietary baseline on the shared eval set.
- Qualitative: hallucination rate (defined as incorrect extractions) <= 2% on sampled production prompts.
- Performance: 95th percentile latency within 2x of current baseline for typical batch sizes (we'll confirm exact batch distribution).

Attachments & links
- I attached the prompt set we'll use and the initial benchmark doc (see attachments). Also sharing the drive folder link in case you want to add other prompts.

Proposed next steps
1) Confirm acceptance thresholds above (or give alternatives).
2) We kick off a 2-week model-fit eval: Redwood runs the benchmark on the three suggested models using your prompt set and production-like traffic.
3) Weekly check-ins (Tuesdays) + final parity report + recommended rolling plan (canary rollout plan if you pick an open model).

Can you confirm the thresholds and that your legal/procurement contact is ok with the data access for the eval? If yes, we’ll schedule the kickoff for early next week.

Thanks — I’ve CC’d Aditya (SE) to own the eval harness + configs.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0125

Attachments: paygrid_prompt_set_v2.jsonl, paygrid_open_vs_baseline_benchmarks.pdf

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Samir Khan <samir.khan@paygrid.com>
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit evaluation - next steps

Thanks Marissa / Samir — quick technical follow-up with what we'll run and how: 

What we'll evaluate (short):
- Metric set: macro F1, precision/recall, exact-match for critical fields (invoice_id, total_amount), and a hallucination indicator computed by disagreement with structured ground truth.
- Benchmarks will include latency/p99 under your nominal concurrency (please confirm typical concurrent requests).

Suggested eval config (initial):
- Models: llama-3-70b-chat (q4_k_m), redopen-13b-v2 (nf4/int8), redopen-7b-chat (nf4/8bit).
- Tokenization & context: 2,048 context window; use prefix caching for repeated customer prompts.
- Inference config: temperature 0.0 for deterministic extractions; top_p 0.95 for classification fallback tests.

Quick notes on parity thresholds (practical framing):
- 5% absolute drop in macro F1 is our suggested negotiating baseline — that keeps user-facing regression small while giving headroom for cost/latency improvements.
- If you require tighter parity (<=2% drop), we recommend an expanded model slate (including proprietary or fine-tuned variants) and a short fine-tuning stage on a held-back subset.

How we'll share results:
- Deliverable: notebook + PDF report with per-field confusion matrices, prompt-level errors, and recommended canary rollout settings.
- We will also include a prioritized list of problematic prompts and suggested prompt-engineering or small-scale fine-tune candidates.

Attachments: eval_harness_instructions.md (runbook + docker commands), paygrid_open_vs_baseline_benchmarks.pdf (initial template).

Command snippet (eval harness)
- docker run --rm -v $(pwd)/data:/data redwood/eval-harness:latest 
  --model llama-3-70b-chat --input /data/paygrid_prompt_set_v2.jsonl --output /data/out_llama70.jsonl --metrics macro_f1,exact_match

Samir: if you can confirm a sample of 5k labelled examples (or grant read access to the eval bucket), we can start right away.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

From: Samir Khan <samir.khan@paygrid.com>

Cc: PayGrid Procurement <procurement@paygrid.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 10:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit evaluation - next steps

Hi Marissa / Aditya —

Appreciate the concise plan. A few quick clarifications from our side before we greenlight: 
1) Data access: we can provide a 5k labelled subset but it contains PII fields; will Redwood need a Data Processing Agreement / SOC2 evidence for the eval bucket access? Procurement is copied.
2) Acceptance thresholds: the 5% macro F1 drop seems reasonable as a starting point — can you confirm which dataset you’ll use for the "hallucination" sampling (random production vs. targeted failure modes)?
3) Timeline & cost: if we run 3 models for 2 weeks, can you give an order-of-magnitude estimate for infra cost (and whether Redwood absorbs eval infra as a trial)?

If we can get answers to the above, procurement can proceed with a short DPA and we’ll plan a kickoff meeting next Tue.

Thanks,
Samir
Head of ML Engineering | PayGrid
samir.khan@paygrid.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Khan <samir.khan@paygrid.com>, PayGrid Procurement <procurement@paygrid.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jun 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: PayGrid model-fit evaluation - next steps

Samir —

Great questions, thanks. Short answers and next-step commitments below: 

1) Data access & compliance: Redwood will sign a short eval DPA. For the eval bucket we can accept a token-limited read-only S3 role scoped to the 5k file sample. Our security team (copied: Neha) will provide SOC2 evidence and a short checklist today.

2) Hallucination sampling: we propose two slices — (A) random production sample (3k) to get a representative metric and (B) targeted failure-mode set (2k) curated by your SMEs focusing on edge cases we saw in the call (multi-currency invoice lines, OCR noise). That combo gives both real-world and stress-case coverage.

3) Timeline & cost: Redwood will cover base infra for the 2-week eval (no charge) — we only ask for a nominal engineering time commitment from PayGrid to provision the eval bucket and bandwith. If you decide to proceed to a longer proof-of-value or Dedicated setup, we’ll provide a formal estimate.

Next steps (confirmable items):
- Procurement: if you can send the short DPA back, we’ll countersign and collect the S3 role.
- Samir: confirm the 5k sample + permission to create the read-only role (we’ll provide the exact ARN).
- Kickoff: proposed Tue Jul 7 10:00 AM PT (30 minutes) — will do a quick handoff and run through the eval plan.

Aditya & Neha: can you prepare the initial run commands + a quick infra checklist before EOD today?

Thanks — looking forward to getting this going.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
